title: Unit Testing and Test Cases
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its role in reliable software.
Identify the topic in code or a realistic scenario.
Trace behavior and describe the expected result.
Apply the concept and verify it using a suitable test.

understand.concept: A unit test checks a small, focused unit—often a function or method—against defined expectations. A test case specifies inputs, conditions, and expected outcomes. Good unit tests are repeatable, isolated where practical, readable, and cover normal, invalid, and boundary behavior.
understand.whyItMatters: Unit tests provide fast feedback on local behavior and help prevent accidental changes from breaking existing expectations.
understand.analogy: Investigating a problem or checking a process uses observations, clear expectations, and controlled steps rather than guesswork.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is a simplification; software behavior depends on runtime, interfaces, and the specific system.

explain.narrative: Define the behavior and expected result before testing. Arrange the data, invoke the unit, and assert the result. Keep tests independent, name them by behavior, and include representative boundary and failure cases. A passing test only verifies its assertion and scenario—not the entire application.

questions.prompt: What is the usual focus of a unit test?
options: A small isolated behavior or unit
Every network connection in the system
questions.answer: A small isolated behavior or unit
questions.explanation: Unit tests focus on small units and their expected behavior.

options: Whether actual behavior matches an expected condition
Whether the source file has a title
Whether the developer likes the code
questions.answer: Whether actual behavior matches an expected condition

questions.prompt: Which test input is valuable besides typical input?
options: No input at all for every function
questions.explanation: Edge and invalid cases often reveal hidden assumptions.

questions.prompt: Why should unit tests be repeatable?
options: Consistent results make failures trustworthy and easier to diagnose
They should depend on random timing
questions.answer: Consistent results make failures trustworthy and easier to diagnose

questions.prompt: Do passing unit tests prove the whole application is correct?
options: No; they only verify covered behaviors and assertions
Yes, every bug is covered automatically
Yes, if there are five tests
questions.answer: No; they only verify covered behaviors and assertions
questions.explanation: Test coverage is limited to what tests actually exercise.
